transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve barely been sleeping since the warehouse inspection. I just lie there replaying parts of it, and when I do fall asleep, I wake up sweaty and completely awake—like I’m back near that blast.
Since the blast, have unwanted memories of it been popping into your mind during the day?
Yes. I’ll be reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and suddenly I see the worker on the floor and the soot in the air. It hits really sharply, and my body reacts before I can stop it.
How long has it been since the warehouse blast?
It’s been about a week now—since that inspection, when the explosion happened.
Since the blast, have you been avoiding reminders of what happened?
Yes. I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file, and I let calls about industrial accounts go to voicemail. Even opening those emails makes my stomach drop.
Have these symptoms continued for a month or more since the blast?
No, it hasn’t been a month. It’s only been about a week, since the warehouse inspection and the explosion.
Since the explosion, have you had moments where it feels like you are actually back there and reliving it?

Yes. During the day, I’ll be looking over a policy or a loss report, and all of a sudden I see the worker on the floor and the soot in the air. It hits me sharply, and my body reacts before I can really stop it.
During the warehouse explosion, did you think you might be killed or seriously injured?
I’m not sure. It happened so fast—I don’t really remember thinking that clearly in the moment.
During or right after the explosion, did you feel intense fear, helplessness, or horror?
I don’t know. I remember being shocked, but I can’t really separate what I felt right then from everything that happened afterward.
Since the explosion, have there been times when you felt detached from yourself, as if you were outside your body watching yourself?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve felt shaken up, but not like I was outside myself watching it happen.
Are there any important parts of what happened during the explosion that you still can’t remember?
Yes. I remember hearing the explosion, and then I remember being outside afterward with soot on my jacket. But everything in between is just blank, no matter how hard I try to piece it together.
Since the explosion, have you been more jumpy or easily startled than usual?

Yes. At work, if a printer jams or a door slams, I jump like something terrible is happening. Even when someone comes up behind my desk, it really startles me, and it takes me a few minutes to calm back down.
Since the explosion, have there been times when you felt emotionally numb, like you couldn’t feel much of anything?
I’m not really sure what you mean. I’ve been upset, but I don’t think I’ve felt completely numb or unable to feel anything.
Since the explosion, have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yes. I’ve missed several deadlines on underwriting reviews, and I’ve started handing off calls for industrial accounts that I’m supposed to handle myself. I just took this role, so it’s making me look unreliable.
At any point during the explosion, did you believe that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?
I’m not sure. I remember being scared, but I can’t really say whether I thought someone was going to die or be seriously hurt.
Have these symptoms been present continuously for more than two days since the explosion?
Yes. It’s been going on for about a week now, ever since the warehouse inspection where the explosion happened.
Since the explosion, have you felt like your future will somehow be cut short?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really felt like my future is going to be cut short.
Since the explosion, have there been times when things around you felt unreal or dreamlike?
I’m not really sure what you mean by unreal or dreamlike. I haven’t noticed that specifically.
Since the explosion, have there been times when you felt dazed or less aware of what was going on around you?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling dazed or less aware of what’s going on around me.
